subject: Order Form: phased prepay proposal + EU VAT reverse-charge clarification
messages:
From: Susan Dunn <susan.dunn@brighthealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify invoicing cadence & VAT reverse-charge for EU entity

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited to move forward. Procurement asked me to confirm two commercial details before we sign the order form:

1) Invoicing cadence for the prepay and subsequent true-up invoices. Our standard is to pay against invoices net 30, but for this contract we may need to confirm how the upfront prepay and phased amounts will be invoiced (single invoice vs split).

2) EU VAT handling: BrightHealth would prefer use of the reverse-charge mechanic if Redwood can issue an invoice without VAT and we can self-account in DE. Can you confirm Redwood's requirement here and whether you need our VAT registration number?

Would appreciate a quick note on the proposed invoice split and any items Redwood needs from our side to accept reverse-charge.

Thanks —
Susan
Susan Dunn
Sr. Procurement Manager | BrightHealth
procurement@brighthealth.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Dunn <susan.dunn@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing cadence & VAT reverse-charge for EU entity

Hi Susan — thanks for flagging. Looping in Kim (billing & tax) and Ben (commercials) to confirm exact language and redlines.

Baseline proposal from our side (see attached proposed-orderform_v1.pdf):
- Prepay phasing: 50% of contracted commitment invoiced at signing (upfront), 25% invoiced at month 6, 25% at month 12. Each prepay invoice will be issued to the BrightHealth DE legal entity on the invoice date.
- Subsequent consumption true-ups (if any) will be invoiced quarterly and follow agreed net terms (we typically request Net 45 for large enterprise billing).
- VAT: Redwood can support reverse-charge (zero-rated VAT on our invoice) provided we receive BrightHealth's VAT registration number and a valid billing entity to put on the invoice. Our tax team may require a clause in the order form that BrightHealth confirms eligibility for reverse-charge and will self-account.

Open asks from our side:
- Do you need the initial upfront invoice split into two documents (accting request) or is one upfront invoice OK?
- Will BrightHealth provide VAT registration and the legal entity name for invoicing?

Ben/Kim — please weigh in on whether the prepay phasing above is acceptable as-is or if we should propose 60/40 upfront vs later. Also anything to add re: contract language to protect Redwood re: withholding or cross-border tax liabilities.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Dunn <susan.dunn@brighthealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing cadence & VAT reverse-charge for EU entity

On Fri, Jun 21, 2028 at 09:28 Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Susan — thanks for flagging. Looping in Kim (billing & tax) and Ben (commercials) to confirm exact language and redlines.
> 
> Baseline proposal from our side (see attached proposed-orderform_v1.pdf):
> - Prepay phasing: 50% upfront, 25% at month 6, 25% at month 12.

Thanks — quick commercial notes from my side (I attached a tracked redline): redlines_orderform_v1.docx

Summary of proposed changes (high level):
- Prepay split: suggest 60% at signing, 40% at month 6 (reduces Redwood working capital risk). If BrightHealth needs 50/25/25 for accounting, we can accept but request a prepay credit mechanism tied to usage to prevent double payment exposure.
- Net terms: propose Net 45 for any post-prepay invoices (true-ups, consumption) rather than Net 30. We can be flexible to Net 30 with a minor price uplift or a payment schedule guarantee.
- VAT / reverse-charge: Kim, please confirm, but our tax ops require: (a) BrightHealth VAT ID on purchase order, (b) explicit statement in the order form that BrightHealth is the reverse-charge liable party and (c) Redwood reserves the right to invoice VAT if a jurisdiction or entity mismatch is discovered.
- Withholding: include a clause that customer will not withhold any taxes from payments made to Redwood unless required by law and then provide official documentation; Redwood will cooperate on gross-up discussions if withholding cannot be avoided.

Attachments: redlines_orderform_v1.docx (word file with tracked changes), short attachment stub: "redlines_orderform_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)"

If these commercial positions are acceptable, I can take the tracked redline to legal for a quick MSA/order form patch.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Director, Commercials | Redwood Inference
From: Susan Dunn <susan.dunn@brighthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightHealth Procurement <procurement@brighthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing cadence & VAT reverse-charge for EU entity

Ben / Evelyn — thanks for the quick turn.

We can accept the 60/40 split if that expedites sign-off; procurement prefers a 50/25/25 but treasury will accept 60/40 if the PO and legal entity are exactly the BrightHealth DE GmbH details. I will provide our VAT registration number and confirm the billing entity by EOD.

Regarding net terms: treasury is pushing for Net 30 on ongoing invoices. If Redwood needs Net 45, can you confirm the price uplift % you would require to move to Net 30? If you prefer to keep Net 45, we can escalate to finance for approval but it's likely to add a couple days.

Also please send over the DocuSign link when the order form redline is ready; procurement needs to attach the PO and the VAT certificates to the envelope.

Best,
Susan
